links.comparator_used: Naive zero-shot GPT-4 without retrieved examples
links.outcome: Prediction of ED admission (AUC, AUPRC, accuracy)
links.effect: Naive GPT-4: 0.79 AUC, 0.48 AUPRC, 77.5% accuracy. RAG alone: 0.82 AUC, 0.56 AUPRC, 81.3% accuracy.
links.quote: Interestingly, RAG alone boosted performance to near peak levels (0.82 AUC, 0.56 AUPRC, and 81.3% accuracy).

links.comparator_used: Naive GPT-4 alone, without ML numerical probabilities
links.outcome: Prediction of ED admission (AUC, AUPRC, accuracy)
links.effect: Naive GPT-4: 0.79 AUC, 0.48 AUPRC, 77.5% accuracy. With RAG and ML probabilities: 0.87 AUC, 0.71 AUPRC, 83.1% accuracy. The pure Ensemble ML model reached 0.88 AUC, 0.72 AUPRC, 82.9% accuracy.
links.tradeoff: Peak LLM performance was still slightly lower than the pure ML model on AUC and AUPRC.
links.quote: The naïve GPT-4's performance (0.79 AUC, 0.48 AUPRC, and 77.5% accuracy) showed substantial improvement when given limited, relevant data to learn from (ie, RAG) and underlying ML probabilities (0.87 AUC, 0.71 AUPRC, and 83.1% accuracy).

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG) and ML probability augmentation of an LLM
